newsitem.title: USA: First State says sets 3-for-2 stock split.
newsitem.headline: First State says sets 3-for-2 stock split.

text.p: First State Corp said on Monday it had approved a 3-for-2 stock split, marking the fourth consecutive year it has announced a split.
The stock split is for shareholders of record May 10 and payable May 20, the company said in a statement.
First State saw its stock rise 86 percent in 1996, and is currently trading between 26 3/4 and 29 7/8 dollars per share, the company said.
It added that it was splitting the stock "to put more shares in the hands of its stockholders, create additional liquidity for the stock, and attract new stockholders to the company.
First State is a two-bank holding company which consists of First State Bank & Trust, Albany, and First State Bank & Trust, Cordele, Georgia.
